text:
SASRec combines item embeddings, learned positions and causal attention; deleting history and compacting survivors therefore changes both evidence and positional distances. Positional-embedding analysis finds strong distance-related structure, making compaction a plausible confound ([Luo et al., 2024](https://arxiv.org/html/2407.02793v1)). Suggested diagnostic controls: compare compacted deletion against deletion that preserves surviving position IDs and masks removed slots as attention keys/values throughout all layers. Keep the final item and readout position fixed. This separates some positional effects, although removal still changes attention normalization; these are proposed controls, not established findings from that paper.

Shuffle only the prefix while preserving its item multiset, occupied slots, length and last item; repeat across permutations. A performance drop supports sensitivity to earlier item placement/order conditional on the last item, but cannot distinguish useful transitions from recency weighting or perturbation-induced distribution shift. An unchanged score does not establish that history is unused: pooled historical evidence can survive shuffling. Compare separately trained last-item, uniformly pooled history, and fixed recency-weighted additive item-to-candidate models. Uniform pooling is order-invariant; recency weighting is not invariant when items move between age slots. A recent controlled comparison found history-aware pairwise models outperforming SASRec/eSASRec on three Amazon benchmarks, demonstrating that useful historical evidence need not require joint history modelling ([Spotify Research, 2026](https://research.atspotify.com/2026/10/do-sequential-recommendation-benchmarks-require-higher-order-sequence-modelling)).

For RecHarness, keep validation users and candidates identical across controls; report paired HR@10 changes, uncertainty and per-category results alongside the macro average. Interpret perturbations as model-sensitivity evidence, not proof of causal user preferences or higher-order reasoning. Published results on other Amazon categories do not establish outcomes for the four requested datasets.
